title: Preventing Burns & Scalds
blurb: The simple kitchen habits that prevent burns and scalds, and what to do straight away if someone is burned.

cards.title: Preventing Burns & Scalds
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- name the hot hazards in a kitchen
- use simple habits to avoid burns and scalds
- treat a burn correctly and report it

cards.title: Burns are common, and preventable
cards.body: A busy kitchen is full of very hot things, so burns and scalds are among the most common kitchen injuries. The good news is that nearly all of them can be prevented with a few good habits and some awareness of what is going on around you.

cards.title: Three habits to start with
cards.body: Start with the simple stuff. A damp or wet cloth conducts heat straight through, so it gives you a scald. Pan handles can be knocked or catch fire if they stick out. Steam comes out fast when you lift a lid.

items.title: Dry oven cloth
items.text: Never damp or wet. Heat passes straight through.

items.title: Handles inwards
items.text: Away from the edge and off the flame.

items.title: Lids away from you
items.text: Open away from your face to let steam out.

cards.title: Call it out, take care with oil
cards.body:
Communication saves skin. Call out clearly when you are moving with something hot, so colleagues can keep clear.

> Hot oil spits. Never add wet food to hot oil, and move hot pans and stockpots slowly and deliberately.

left.title: Do
items: Take real care at the fryer

right.title: Do not
items: Add wet food to hot oil

cards.title: Act fast
cards.body: If someone gets burned, act fast. For anything more than a minor burn, get first aid, and for a serious burn get medical help. Then report it so we can prevent the next one.

items.title: Cool it
items.text: Cool running water, not ice-cold, for at least 20 minutes.

items.title: Jewellery off
items.text: Remove watches or rings near the burn before it swells.

items.title: No butter
items.text: Do not put butter or creams on it.

items.title: Get help, report
items.text: First aid, medical help if serious, then report.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Use a dry oven cloth, never a damp one
- Handles inwards, lids open away from your face
- Call out when you carry something hot
- Cool a burn under running water for at least 20 minutes
- Report every burn so we can stop the next one

cards.q: A damp or wet oven cloth can give you a scald.
cards.why: Damp or wet cloth conducts heat straight through to your hand, which gives you a nasty scald. Always use a dry one.

cards.q: Which way should pan handles point?
options: Outwards, so they are easy to grab
Inwards, away from the edge and off the flame
Over the edge of the hob to save space
Towards the next pan to keep things tidy
cards.why: Handles turned inwards, away from the edge and off the flame, cannot be knocked or catch fire.

cards.q: When opening a hot lid or pan, open it…
options: Towards your face, to see inside
Directly above the pan
Away from your face
Very fast, to get it over with
cards.why: Opening away from your face lets the steam escape safely instead of scalding you.

cards.q: Calling out "hot behind!" helps prevent burns.
cards.why: Calling out when you are moving with something hot lets colleagues keep clear. Communication saves skin.

cards.q: How should you treat a burn?
options: Put butter on it to soothe it
Hold ice directly on it
Cool running water for at least 20 minutes
A cold damp cloth for a minute or two
cards.why: Cool the burn under cool, not ice-cold, running water for at least 20 minutes. Butter and creams should not be used.

cards.q: You should add wet food to hot oil to cool it down.
cards.why: Never add wet food to hot oil. It spits and can cause serious burns.

cards.q: Why remove rings or a watch from a burned hand quickly?
options: So the metal does not get lost in the sink
So a cream can be rubbed in
So the burn can be photographed
Before the area swells
cards.why: Remove watches or rings near the burn before it swells, when they would be much harder to take off.
Nearly all burns and scalds can be prevented with a few good habits and awareness of what is going on around you.

cards.q: Which oven cloth should you use?
options: One soaked in cold water to keep your hands cool
A dry one
A damp one, so it does not scorch
Whichever is nearest, wet or dry
cards.why: Always use a dry cloth. A damp or wet one conducts heat straight through and gives you a scald.

cards.q: Butter or creams are a good first-aid treatment for a burn.
cards.why: Do not put butter or creams on a burn. Cool it under running water instead.
